newsitem.title: UK: UK SFO considers investigation into NatWest.
newsitem.headline: UK SFO considers investigation into NatWest.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO), which investigates cases of complex and serious financial fraud, said on Thursday it is considering whether there are sufficient grounds for it to launch an investigation into options losses at NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank.

A spokesman for the SFO told Reuters that it had been monitoring the situation and had received briefings from NatWest on its report into the affair, published on Thursday, in which the bank said there had been deliberate concealment of the losses which amounted to 90 million pounds ($150 million).

The SFO spokesman said the Office's director, Rosalind Wright, can decide to launch an investigation into a case "where, on reasonable grounds, there is a suspicion that a serious or complex fraud may have taken place."
He added that the SFO hopes to have gathered enough information in the next few weeks to decide whether a criminal investigation will be launched.
The affair centres around options trader Kyriacos Papouis, who left NatWest in December 1996, who, according to NatWest, "...covered up losses and created false profits over two years."

NatWest said on Thursday that five senior NatWest staff have resigned over the affair, which has already caused the departure of NatWest Markets chief executive Martin Owen. ($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
